narrative.text: BioSense was asked to increase viable macrophage production while maintaining macrophage identity and viability.
It identified an unresolved question: Nothing in this project says whether the current M-CSF concentration is limiting the monocyte yield, so a revision would move it blind.
It found 1 relevant dataset(s) already registered.
Comparing the conditions in that data, cd14 pos pct goes from 41.18% to 67.58%, a change of +26.4 percentage points (+64.1%) — calculated from measurements.
BioSense proposes that M-CSF is worth testing.
Testing that in the project simulator, monocytes per input ipsc goes from 17.99 cells/input_cell to 29.66 cells/input_cell, a change of +11.67 cells/input_cell (+64.87%) — predicted by the simulator.

Temperature could not be simulated: temperature_c is a real design variable in ipsc_macrophage but its simulator has no term for it, so no prediction is produced. A real process parameter. The model holds temperature fixed, so changing it here produces no prediction.
